newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q4 non-farm productivity +2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q4 non-farm productivity +2.2 pct.

text.p: Labor estimates of U.S. productivity/costs, seasonally adjusted annual percent changes from prior quarters, on chain weights basis (1992=100):
- Q4-P Q3 Q2 Q4-P Q3 Q2
- Q4-P Q3 Q2 Q4-P Q3 Q2
- Real Hourly Compensation Unit Labor Costs
- Q4-P Q3 Q2 Q4-P Q3 Q2
Wall Street economists had forecast fourth-quarter non-farm productivity to increase 2.1 percent, and unit labor costs to be up 1.4 percent.

Compared to the fourth quarter 1995, fourth quarter 1996 non-farm productivity rose 1.2 percent, output grew 3.8 percent, hours rose 2.6 percent, hourly compensation increased 3.6 percent, real hourly compensation rose 0.4 percent and unit labor costs gained 2.4 percent.
For all of 1996, nonfarm productivity rose 0.8 percent after rising 0.3 percent in 1995. Nonfarm unit labor costs in 1996 rose 2.9 percent, after a 2.9 percent rise in 1995, the department said.
The department said the gain in fourth-quarter nonfarm productivity was the biggest since a 2.8 percent increase in the fourth quarter of 1993.
